cameras:

    enabled: true
    live:
      streams:
        front_door_fullres: front_door_fullres
    ffmpeg:
      output_args:
        record: preset-record-generic-audio-aac
      inputs:
        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/front_door
          roles:
            - detect
        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/front_door_fullres?video&audio
          roles:
            - record
    detect:
      width: 640
      height: 480
      fps: 5
    snapshots:
      enabled: true
      required_zones:
        - porch
    record:
      enabled: true

        # required_zones:
        #   - porch
    # rtmp:

    motion:

        - 519,480,640,480,640,480,640,480,640,90,640,0,518,0,525,276
        - 0,255,0,165,640,158,640,254
        - 0,236,640,230,640,0,0,0
    zones:
      porch:
        coordinates: 0,480,517,480,525,264,0,229
        objects:
          - person

    ffmpeg:

        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/garage_sub?video&audio

            - detect
        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/garage?video&audio
          roles:
            - record

      width: 640
      height: 480
      fps: 5
    snapshots:
      enabled: true
    record:
      enabled: true

        # required_zones:
        #   - porch

    #   enabled: false
    motion:
      mask: 0.72,0.918,0.979,0.915,0.981,0.991,0.721,0.99
  back_door:
    enabled: true
    ffmpeg:
      output_args:
        record: preset-record-generic-audio-aac
      inputs:
        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/back_door_sub?video&audio
          roles:
            - detect
        - path: rtsp://127.0.0.1:8554/back_door?video&audio
          roles:
            - record
    detect:
      width: 640
      height: 480
      fps: 5
    snapshots:
      enabled: true
    record:
      enabled: true
detectors:
  cpu1:
    type: cpu
record:
  # Optional: Enable recording (default: shown below)
  enabled: true
  # Optional: Number of days to retain recordings regardless of events (default: shown below)

  # Optional: Event recording settings
  alerts:
    retain:
      days: 10
    pre_capture: 5
    post_capture: 5
  detections:
    retain:
      days: 10
    pre_capture: 5
    post_capture: 5

/hr/ghcr.io-kubereboot-charts-kured.name: kured
/hr/ghcr.io-kubereboot-charts-kured.doc: Kured (Kubernetes REboot Daemon) is a Kubernetes add-on that automates the process of rebooting nodes in your cluster. It integrates with the underlying operating system's package management system to identify when a reboot is necessary, and performs the reboot in a safe and controlled manner to minimize disruption to your applications.

# remap app name from label
.custom_app_name = .pod_labels."app.kubernetes.io/name" || .pod_labels.app || .pod_labels."k8s-app" || "unknown"
# remap pod name from event
.custom_pod_name = .pod_name || "unknown"
# drop remapped fields
del(.pod_labels)

/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.title: redis helm release
/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.name: redis
/hr/bjw-s-labs.github.io-helm-charts-app.doc:
Redis is an open-source, in-memory data structure store that is used as a database, cache, and message broker. It provides a fast and flexible solution for storing and retrieving data, making it an ideal choice for a wide range of use cases, including real-time analytics, session management, and more.

Redis is used by Authentik, Authelia, oauth2-proxy.
